why: The first real accumulation in the storage family. Two work reports become available (enough validators assured them), the service's accumulate code runs in the PVM for 478,680 gas, writes storage, and the accumulated-set ring C(15) records the package hashes.
family_explainer: The storage family runs a real service that stress-tests service storage. Each block: (1) new work reports are guaranteed onto cores, (2) validators assure availability of earlier reports, (3) once a report has a super-majority of assurances it becomes available and the service's ACCUMULATE entry point executes in the PVM — reading, writing and deleting storage keys via host calls, metered by gas. The post-state root certifies every byte: storage entries, the service's octet/item footprint, gas statistics, the accumulated-set ring and the ready queue.
events: Core 0: package a93f2452… guaranteed (1 work item(s), bundle 1090 bytes) — declares prerequisite 585fd824…. It now waits on this core for availability assurances.
Core 1: package 31bf7582… guaranteed (5 work item(s), bundle 4125 bytes) — declares prerequisite 585fd824…. It now waits on this core for availability assurances.
6 validator assurance(s): core 0 has 5, core 1 has 6 vote(s). A report becomes AVAILABLE when votes exceed 2/3 of 6 validators (i.e. ≥ 5).

ACCUMULATION: package(s) 585fd824…, a80fc6bb… became available and were accumulated — the service's accumulate entry point ran inside the PVM. The accumulated-set ring C(15) records them (sorted, ring 11), aging out after 12 blocks.
Service 0 statistics: 3 work item(s) accumulated for 478,680 gas (exact PVM metering — every instruction costs 1, host calls cost 10, log costs 10).
